items.title: Region XII Validates Community Heritage Learning Centers in Kidapawan City
items.tags: community heritage learning centers CHLC validation Kidapawan City IPEd indigenous peoples education cultural heritage IP knowledge Dagadas Nungauan Ginantilan Balabag
items.summary: DepEd Region XII conducted the Regional Validation of Community Heritage Learning Centers (CHLC) in SDO Kidapawan on September 22–23, 2026, assessing the readiness, functionality, and cultural relevance of identified sites in Nungauan, Ginantilan, and Balabag as community-based spaces for preserving and transmitting Indigenous Peoples’ knowledge and heritage.
body: KIDAPAWAN CITY, COTABATO — The Department of Education (DepEd) Region XII conducted the Regional Validation of Community Heritage Learning Centers (CHLC) in the Schools Division Office (SDO) of Kidapawan on September 22–23, 2026, covering identified sites in Nungauan, Ginantilan, and Balabag.

The validation team was composed of Regional IPED Focal Person Regan B. Dagadas, Chief Education Program Specialist Norman Valeroso, Education Program Supervisor Leonardo Mission, Crisanto Bulado, and Education Program Supervisor Ildefonso E. Libdan, in coordination with SDO Kidapawan IPED Focal Person Lama Belarmino.

The activity aimed to validate the readiness, functionality, cultural relevance, and learning potential of identified Community Heritage Learning Centers as community-based spaces for preserving, promoting, and transmitting Indigenous Peoples’ (IP) knowledge, traditions, practices, histories, and cultural heritage.

The initiative recognizes the importance of bringing learning beyond the conventional classroom by providing learners with opportunities to engage with their communities and experience culture and heritage in authentic settings. CHLCs can serve as meaningful learning spaces where indigenous knowledge and local cultural resources are integrated into educational experiences.

During the two-day validation, the regional team conducted on-site assessment, documentation, consultation, and observation of the identified CHLC sites. The team examined the learning environment, available cultural resources, community participation, potential learning applications, and other considerations relevant to the establishment and functionality of the centers.

The validation was also undertaken through dialogue and coordination with local stakeholders and the SDO Kidapawan IPED team, ensuring that community perspectives and cultural considerations are reflected in the assessment process.

The activity forms part of DepEd Region XII’s continuing efforts to strengthen Indigenous Peoples Education (IPEd), promote culturally responsive education, and support the preservation and meaningful integration of local and indigenous heritage in the learning process.

Through the regional validation, DepEd Region XII seeks to help ensure that Community Heritage Learning Centers become responsive, culturally grounded, and meaningful spaces for learning, while strengthening partnerships among schools, communities, and Indigenous Peoples in safeguarding their living heritage.

items.title: Kidapawan City Readies for Region XII’s 2026 Science and Technology Fair
items.tags: science technology fair RSTF Kidapawan City planning conference post-evaluation site inspection billeting LGU innovation December 2026
items.summary: DepEd Region XII and the LGU of Kidapawan City intensify preparations for the 2026 Regional Science and Technology Fair (RSTF) on December 12–13, 2026, with the regional science team completing planning and site inspections during the RSTF Post-Evaluation and Planning Conference.
body: KIDAPAWAN CITY, COTABATO — Kidapawan City is gearing up to host the 2026 Regional Science and Technology Fair (RSTF) as DepEd Region XII and the Local Government Unit (LGU) of Kidapawan City intensify preparations for the region’s premier science and technology showcase on December 12–13, 2026.

The preparations gained momentum during the second day of the 2026 RSTF Post-Evaluation and Planning Conference, highlighted by a courtesy call and presentation to the local executive officials of the LGU of Kidapawan City. The engagement reaffirmed the local government’s support and commitment to the successful conduct of the regional event.

Leading the regional science team was Education Program Supervisor (EPS) Dantly S. Villanueva, Regional EPS in Science, together with the Education Program Supervisors in Science from the eight Schools Division Offices (SDOs) of Region XII. Their participation strengthened the region-wide coordination and collaborative planning necessary for the successful implementation of the RSTF.

As part of the preparations, the team conducted site visits to proposed billeting quarters and display rooms to assess their suitability and readiness for participating learners, coaches, teachers, and officials. The proposed venue for the RSTF 2026 Opening Program was likewise inspected as part of the comprehensive preparations for the event.

The planning and site-inspection activities are designed to ensure that essential arrangements—from billeting and exhibition spaces to the opening program venue—are systematically addressed well ahead of the regional fair.

Set for December 12–13, 2026, in Kidapawan City, the RSTF will bring together young science enthusiasts and innovators from across SOCCSKSARGEN to showcase their scientific inquiry, creativity, innovation, and technological skills.

With the continued collaboration of DepEd Region XII, the eight SDOs, and the LGU of Kidapawan City, preparations are steadily taking shape toward an organized, meaningful, and successful Regional Science and Technology Fair 2026.

items.title: DepEd Region XII Holds 2026 Regional Work Immersion Fair to Strengthen School-Industry Alliances
items.tags: work immersion fair Senior High School industry partnership school-industry alliances SHS learners technical vocational skills Libertad National High School South Cotabato employment workforce readiness
items.summary: DepEd Region XII gathered educational leaders, local government officials, and industry executives at Libertad National High School on September 18, 2026 for the 2026 Regional Work Immersion Fair, bridging classroom instruction and real-world employment for Senior High School learners.
body: LIBERTAD, SOUTH COTABATO — The Department of Education (DepEd) Region XII gathered key educational leaders, local government officials, and industry executives at Libertad National High School on September 18, 2026, for the 2026 Regional Work Immersion Fair, aimed at bridging the gap between classroom instruction and real-world employment.

Anchored on the theme "Bridging Aspiration and Opportunity: Strengthening Industry-School Partnerships," the event emphasized the critical role of corporate and community collaboration in preparing Senior High School (SHS) students for tertiary education, entrepreneurship, and immediate workforce entry.

The regional gathering brought together high-ranking officials, including Assistant Secretary Janir T. Datukan, Assistant Regional Director Kathrine H. Lotilla, Schools Division Superintendent Leonardo M. Balala, and Surallah Mayor Pedro Matinong Jr., alongside local industry partners across various economic sectors.

The initiative was spearheaded by the DepEd Region XII team, led by Chief Shienna Lyn L. Antenor, together with Regional Education Program Supervisors and Education Program Supervisors (EPSs) representing all eight Schools Division Offices (SDOs) in the region.

Throughout the day-long fair, stakeholders participated in partnership forums, Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) ceremonial signings, and interactive career exhibits. SHS learners were given direct opportunities to display their technical-vocational skills and capstone innovations to potential employers.

Speaking on the core objective of the fair, organizers underscored that the event serves as a strategic catalyst for long-term regional development. By matching curriculum competencies with the actual skill requirements of local industries, DepEd Region XII aims to equip Senior High School graduates with actionable career pathways, sustainable innovation capabilities, and workforce readiness.

items.title: Region XII Launches 2026 Search for the Most Functional Library
items.tags: school library most functional library search learning resources validation librarians reading information literacy Region XII
items.summary: DepEd Region XII strengthens school library services through the 2026 Search for the Most Functional Library (September 15–29, 2026), recognizing functional, learner-centered, and well-managed school libraries across the region.
body: SOCCSKSARGEN — DepEd Region XII is stepping up efforts to strengthen school library services through the 2026 Search for the Most Functional Library, being conducted from September 15 to 29, 2026 in identified schools with libraries across the region.

Spearheading the regional initiative are Education Program Supervisor for Learning Resources Arturo Tingson and Regional Librarian Jeannette Militante, together with the Education Program Supervisors, Division Learning Resources Supervisors, and Division Librarians from the Schools Division Offices across Region XII.

The search aims to recognize and promote functional, learner-centered, accessible, and well-managed school libraries that effectively contribute to teaching and learning. Beyond identifying exemplary libraries, the initiative seeks to showcase innovative practices that encourage reading, information literacy, independent learning, and meaningful utilization of learning resources.

During the validation, participating schools are assessed based on key aspects of library functionality, including facilities and learning environment, organization and management of resources, accessibility and utilization, library programs and services, and innovative practices.

Regional and Division Learning Resources personnel and librarians are conducting the assessment and validation, documenting effective practices and gathering evidence that may serve as models for other schools.

More than a search for recognition, the initiative provides an opportunity for schools to reflect on their library services, identify areas for improvement, and share practices that make learning resources more accessible and meaningful to learners and teachers.

Through the 2026 Search for the Most Functional Library, DepEd Region XII continues to promote school libraries as dynamic learning spaces—places where resources, readers, and opportunities for lifelong learning come together.

items.title: Learners Turn Food Advocacy into Art at Regional World Food Day Contest
items.tags: World Food Day poster making on-the-spot contest food security nutrition sustainable food systems learners Greenleaf Hotel General Santos City Department of Agriculture
items.summary: Twenty-four learners from the Schools Divisions of Region XII transformed their ideas on food security, nutrition, and sustainable food systems into vibrant works of art during the Regional World Food Day On-the-Spot Poster-Making Contest at Greenleaf Hotel, General Santos City on September 19, 2026.
body: GENERAL SANTOS CITY, September 19, 2026 — Twenty-four learners from the Schools Divisions of Region XII transformed their ideas on food security, nutrition, and sustainable food systems into vibrant works of art during the Regional World Food Day On-the-Spot Poster-Making Contest held at Greenleaf Hotel, General Santos City.

Supported by the Department of Education (DepEd) Region XII and the Department of Agriculture (DA), the activity provided learners with a creative platform to express their understanding of the importance of safe, nutritious, and accessible food for all.

Representing their respective Schools Divisions, the participating learners created their posters on the spot, demonstrating both artistic skill and awareness of the significance of World Food Day. Their works translated messages on food security, healthy nutrition, sustainable agriculture, and collective responsibility into visual stories.

The activity also brought together Education Program Supervisors and education personnel who supported the learners and reinforced the value of meaningful advocacy activities that develop creativity, communication, and social awareness.
Following the evaluation of the entries based on the prescribed contest criteria, the Schools Division Office of South Cotabato was declared Champion, with SDO General Santos City as 2nd Runner-Up.

Beyond the competition, the Regional World Food Day activity highlighted how art can serve as a powerful medium for advocacy, giving young people an opportunity to communicate messages that encourage awareness and action toward a food-secure and nourished community.

items.title: MAPEH Teachers Across SOCCSKSARGEN Unite to Localize Grade 6 Revised K–10 Curriculum
items.tags: MAPEH teachers Grade 6 revised K to 10 curriculum localization contextualization learning resources assessment tools Koronadal
items.summary: MAPEH teachers from the eight Schools Division Offices of DepEd Region XII gathered on September 11–12, 2026 at Viajera Cafe and Dine, Koronadal City for the Regional Training Workshop on Responsive Delivery and Localization of Grade 6 Revised K–10 MAPEH Curriculum Competencies, Learning Resources and Assessment Tools.
body: KORONADAL CITY, SOUTH COTABATO — MAPEH teachers from the eight Schools Division Offices (SDOs) of DepEd Region XII came together on September 11–12, 2026, at Viajera Cafe and Dine for the Regional Training Workshop on Responsive Delivery and Localization of Grade 6 Revised K–10 MAPEH Curriculum Competencies, Learning Resources and Assessment Tools.

The two-day workshop provided a collaborative platform for MAPEH teachers across SOCCSKSARGEN to strengthen the responsive delivery of the Grade 6 Revised K–10 MAPEH Curriculum by integrating the region’s diverse cultural, artistic, musical, physical, health, and community contexts into teaching and learning.

Anchored on the principle of localization and contextualization, the activity aimed to ensure that curriculum contents are delivered in ways that are meaningful and relevant to learners in the region. Participants worked collaboratively in examining curriculum competencies and developing learning resources and assessment tools that reflect the realities, experiences, traditions, and available resources within their respective local communities.

The workshop also highlighted the value of drawing from the rich cultural heritage of SOCCSKSARGEN as a resource for MAPEH instruction. Local music, arts, dances, indigenous practices, community experiences, and health and physical activity contexts were considered in designing learning experiences that can help learners connect classroom concepts with their immediate environment.

With teachers representing the eight SDOs, the workshop encouraged the sharing of practices and locally grounded ideas, allowing participants to learn from the varied contexts of schools across the region. The collaborative process likewise promoted the development of learning resources and assessment tools that are aligned with the curriculum while remaining responsive to learners’ needs and contexts.

items.title: Regional Training for Multigrade Teachers Strengthens Implementation of Revised K to 10 Curriculum
items.tags: multigrade teachers revised K to 10 curriculum training Koronadal Habi Hotel last-mile schools
items.summary: DepEd Region XII is holding a five-day Regional Training for Multigrade Teachers (September 7-11, 2026, Habi Hotel, Koronadal City) to strengthen the implementation of the Revised K to 10 Curriculum in last-mile multigrade schools.
body: The Department of Education (DepEd) Region XII is conducting a Regional Training for Multigrade Teachers from September 7 to 11, 2026, at Habi Hotel, City of Koronadal, aimed at strengthening teachers’ capacity to effectively implement the Revised K to 10 Curriculum in last-mile multigrade (MG) schools.

The five-day training provides multigrade teachers with opportunities to deepen their understanding of the revised curriculum and enhance their instructional practices in addressing the varied academic abilities, learning needs, values, interests, and learning styles of learners within a single classroom.

Through collaborative learning sessions, workshops, and contextualized instructional activities, the training equips teachers with practical strategies for managing multigrade classrooms and delivering meaningful, inclusive, and developmentally appropriate learning experiences.

The initiative underscores DepEd Region XII’s commitment to ensuring that learners in last-mile schools, regardless of location or learning context, receive quality education aligned with the goals of the Revised K to 10 Curriculum.

By strengthening the knowledge, skills, and confidence of multigrade teachers, the training seeks to empower them to create responsive classrooms where every learner can participate, progress, and thrive — Maria Isabel R. Cunanan, EPS CLMD.

items.title: DepEd Region XII Strengthens Arabic Language Instruction Through Two-Year Enhancement Program for Asatidz
items.tags: ALEP asatidz ALIVE Arabic language madrasah General Santos City
items.summary: Launched in partnership with Kulliyat Sugoda Buayan Lidirasatol Islamiyah in General Santos City, the two-year Arabic Language Enhancement Program (ALEP) sharpens the Arabic proficiency and instructional competence of Regular and COS Asatidz/ALIVE teachers across SOCCSKSARGEN.
body: GENERAL SANTOS CITY — September 4, 2026. The Department of Education (DepEd) Region XII, through the Curriculum and Learning Management Division (CLMD), has launched the Arabic Language Enhancement Program (ALEP) for Regular and Contract of Service (COS) Asatidz/ALIVE teachers in partnership with Kulliyat Sugoda Buayan Lidirasatol Islamiyah in General Santos City.

The activity was graced by Assistant Regional Director (ARD) Kathrine H. Lotilla, who joined education leaders, program implementers, partners, and participating Asatidz in advancing initiatives that strengthen the delivery of Madrasah Education.

Anchored on DepEd Order No. 041, s. 2017, or the Policy Guidelines on Madrasah Education in the K to 12 Basic Education Program, the initiative provides a two-year Diploma Course cum Learning and Development Intervention designed to enhance the Arabic language proficiency and instructional competence of Asatidz/ALIVE teachers.

The program aims to improve teachers’ spoken and written Arabic, with emphasis on accuracy, fluency, and clarity, particularly in teaching Qur’an Reading, Islamic Studies, Arabic Grammar, and Modern Standard Arabic (Fusha). It also seeks to deepen teachers’ mastery of basic and complex Arabic language structures and their application in delivering the ALIVE curriculum.

The two-year program will utilize a blended learning approach, combining face-to-face sessions, modular activities, and weekly online synchronous sessions, providing participants with sustained opportunities to develop and apply their language competencies.

Through this initiative, DepEd Region XII reinforces its commitment to quality, inclusive, culturally responsive, and context-sensitive education, recognizing the vital role of competent Asatidz in providing meaningful learning experiences for Muslim learners.

items.title: DepEd Region XII Develops Interactive Video Lessons to Boost Learner Engagement
items.tags: Kinder interactive video lessons Araling Panlipunan Habi Hotel Koronadal DepEd Region XII
items.summary: Education personnel and learning resource developers from DepEd Region XII convened at Habi Hotel, City of Koronadal, from September 3 to 6, 2026, to develop interactive video lessons for Kindergarten and Araling Panlipunan that make learning more engaging, accessible, and responsive.
body: KORONADAL CITY, September 3, 2026 — Education personnel and learning resource developers from DepEd Region XII are convening at Habi Hotel, City of Koronadal, from September 3 to 6, 2026, for the Development of Interactive Video Lessons in Kindergarten and Araling Panlipunan.
The four-day activity aims to develop interactive video lessons designed to make learning more engaging, accessible, and responsive to the diverse needs of learners.

The development initiative focuses on integrating interactive and multimedia elements into lessons to encourage active learner participation while providing opportunities for differentiated instruction. Through carefully designed video lessons, learners are expected to experience more meaningful and age-appropriate learning activities suited to their varying levels of readiness, interests, and learning needs.

For Kindergarten, the interactive video lessons are envisioned to provide developmentally appropriate and engaging learning experiences that stimulate young learners through visuals, sounds, movement, and interactive activities. Meanwhile, the Araling Panlipunan materials will support learners in understanding concepts and issues through contextualized, engaging, and learner-centered presentations.
The activity also underscores the importance of developing quality learning resources that can complement teachers’ classroom instruction and promote learner engagement across the region.

items.title: Teaching Behind Bars: Regional Training of Jail Instructional Managers on the Revised ALS Curriculum
items.tags: BJMP ALS jail instructional managers PDL DepEd Region XII Koronadal Habi Hotel
items.summary: DepEd SOCCSKSARGEN and BJMP Region XII conducted a three-day regional training on the Revised ALS Curriculum for jail officers serving as Instructional Managers, bringing learning to persons deprived of liberty.
body: The Department of Education (DepEd)-SOCCSKSARGEN Region successfully conducted the Regional Training on the Revised Alternative Learning System (ALS) Curriculum for BJMP Jail Officers (Instructional Managers) on August 31 to September 2, 2026, at Habi Hotel, City of Koronadal.

The three-day training aimed to strengthen the knowledge and skills of jail Instructional Managers in supporting the education of persons deprived of liberty (PDLs) through the Alternative Learning System. The participants learned about the key features, learning areas, and implementation of the Revised ALS Curriculum, and were introduced to strategies for supporting learners with different educational backgrounds, needs, and learning experiences.

The training emphasized the importance of ALS in providing education to individuals who were unable to complete their formal schooling. Through ALS programs in jail facilities, PDLs are given opportunities to continue their education, develop important skills, and prepare for their eventual return to their families and communities.

The activity strengthened the partnership between Department of Education–Region XII and the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology–Region XII. As Instructional Managers, the jail officers help create a safe and supportive environment in which PDL learners can participate in learning activities.

Participants took part in discussions, workshops, and group activities that helped them understand how the Revised ALS Curriculum can be applied in jail-based learning settings. The sessions also highlighted their important role in assisting and supporting ALS learners. The training concluded with the participants’ commitment to apply their learning and strengthen the implementation of ALS programs in their respective jail facilities.

Through this initiative, DepEd SOCCSKSARGEN and BJMP reaffirm their commitment to making education accessible to all, including persons deprived of liberty (PDLs), and to using education as a means of personal growth, rehabilitation, and successful reintegration into the community.

items.title: Building Foundations: Enhancing Early Literacy and Numeracy with Khan Academy (Batch 3)
items.tags: khan academy literacy numeracy digital learning training Koronadal Paraiso Verde
items.summary: Educators from across the region assembled at Paraiso Verde, Koronadal City, on August 29, 2026 for a hands-on workshop on the Khan Academy platform — navigating learning materials, designing targeted assessments, and monitoring learner progress in real time.
body: KORONADAL CITY, SOUTH COTABATO — Educators from across the area assembled at Paraiso Verde on August 29, 2026, to participate in the “Building Foundations: Enhancing Early Literacy and Numeracy with Khan Academy (Batch 3)” training workshop. Led by speaker Jay-ar S. Lipura, the session marked another step forward in regional efforts to integrate digital platforms into early childhood education.

The primary objective of the session was to give teacher participants a hands-on understanding of the Khan Academy platform and its capabilities. Throughout the day, educators explored how to navigate the system, access learning materials, design targeted assessments, and utilize real-time progress monitoring tools to keep track of student growth.

By mastering these digital features, participating teachers are now equipped to supplement traditional classroom instruction with technology-driven learning. The initiative ultimately aims to strengthen foundational reading and math skills in early learners, ensuring local educators can effectively adapt interactive platforms to meet the needs of their students.

items.title: No Learner Left Behind: Sultan Kudarat Opens Inclusive Learning Resource Center
items.tags: ILRC Isulan inclusive education SPED Sultan Kudarat learners with disabilities assistive resources
items.summary: The Inclusive Learning Resource Center was formally inaugurated at the Isulan Central School SPED Center, expanding specialized support for learners with disabilities across SOCCSKSARGEN.
body: ISULAN, SULTAN KUDARAT — August 27, 2026. In a significant step toward advancing inclusive education, the Inclusive Learning Resource Center (ILRC) was formally inaugurated at the Isulan Central School SPED Center, bringing together education leaders, local government officials, stakeholders, and professional partners in a shared commitment to support learners with disabilities.

The inauguration was attended by representatives from the Curriculum and Learning Management Division (CLMD) and Human Resource Development Division (HRDD) of the Regional Office, the Schools Division Office of Sultan Kudarat Top Management, SNED Focals from the 8 SDOs of SOCCSKSARGEN Region, the Local Government Unit (LGU), and various stakeholders and professional partners.

The ILRC is envisioned as a responsive hub providing specialized services, appropriate learning tools, assistive resources, technology, and support systems to help learners with disabilities access and participate meaningfully in the learning process.

More than a physical facility, the ILRC embodies the shared commitment to make education accessible, responsive, and inclusive for every learner. It aims to remove barriers to learning by ensuring that learners can access and benefit from resources and support suited to their needs.

“Building an inclusive learning resource center means ensuring that every learner can access, use, and benefit from the space, resources, technology, and support regardless of ability or circumstance,” said CLMD Chief Shienna Lyn L. Antenor.

Through strong partnerships among schools, families, government agencies, stakeholders, and professional organizations, the ILRC marks another meaningful step toward an education system where every learner is seen, supported, valued, and given the opportunity to succeed.

items.title: Day 2 of the CLMD-CID Assembly: Aligning Directions for Quality Education
items.tags: clmd cid assembly day 2 policy alignment quality education planning deped orders
items.summary: CLMD and CID leaders continued collaborative discussions and planning to align division directions with key Department of Education policies and programs.
body: KORONADAL CITY, August 19, 2026 — The second day of the CLMD-CID Assembly brought together Curriculum and Learning Management Division and Curriculum Implementation Division leaders at The Farm @ Carpenter Hills, Koronadal City. CID Chiefs, Education Program Supervisors, and Public School District Supervisors from Schools Division Offices across Region XII continued their collaborative discussions and planning.

The assembly served as an important venue for aligning plans and strategies to support the effective implementation of key Department of Education policies and programs in the respective Schools Division Offices.

Among the major policy issuances discussed were DepEd Order No. 14, s. 2026 on Education in Emergencies; DepEd Order No. 15, s. 2026 on Assessment; DepEd Order No. 16, s. 2026 on Lesson Planning; and DepEd Order No. 17, s. 2026 on Strengthened Senior High School.

The discussions provided CID Chiefs with opportunities to clarify directions, share insights and experiences, and align their division plans with the latest national policies and priorities of the Department.

Other significant topics included Inclusive Education, Special Curricular Programs, and updates on Learning Resources, highlighting the Region’s continuing commitment to curriculum implementation that responds to diverse learner needs and supports quality, inclusive, and relevant education.

As discussions progressed, CID Chiefs worked toward translating key takeaways into concrete and responsive plans for their respective Schools Division Offices. The gathering emphasized collaboration, shared understanding, and unified action among education leaders.

The event photographs document CID Chief Ronela Molina discussing plans for SDO Kidapawan, CID Chief Randy E. Porras sharing plans for SDO Tacurong, and planning sessions involving personnel from Sultan Kudarat, South Cotabato, and General Santos City.

Through sustained coordination and alignment, the CLMD-CID Assembly continues to strengthen the collective efforts of the Regional Office and Schools Division Offices toward a more responsive, inclusive, and learner-centered delivery of education.

items.title: CLMD, CID Unite to Drive Effective Implementation of Policies and Reforms
items.tags: clmd cid assembly convergence strengthened senior high school sshs policy reforms bulletin
items.summary: The CLMD-CID Assembly cum Convergence strengthened coordination, policy understanding, and technical support for implementation in schools across SOCCSKSARGEN.
body: To ensure that policies and reforms are translated, clearly communicated, and effectively implemented in the field, DepEd SOCCSKSARGEN, through the Curriculum Learning Management Division, conducted the CLMD-CID Assembly cum Convergence on the Implementation of Strengthened Senior High School on August 18–19.

More than a venue for policy discussions, the activity gave CLMD and CID an opportunity to work more closely together. By listening to the field, sharing experiences, and clarifying policies, both offices strengthened their commitment to move in the same direction in implementing DepEd reforms.

One highlight was the launching of the CLMD Bulletin, a real-time dashboard that captures projects, programs, memoranda, and other important data accessible to Schools Division Offices, providing timely and relevant information to support program implementation.

Crisanto Bulado, Education Program Supervisor in charge of Strengthened Senior High School, provided policy updates and clarifications. He addressed queries and concerns raised by school heads implementing SSHS, CID Chiefs, and Public Schools District Supervisors to support a common understanding of the reforms at school level.

Program holders listened to the experiences, concerns, and insights of stakeholders in the field. They shared updates and provided technical assistance on lesson planning, the three-term calendar, Education in Emergencies, FLP, classroom assessment, the ARAL Program, Special Programs, Learning Resources, SNED, IPEd, ALIVE, Multigrade, Kindergarten, and SSHS.
Chief Shienna Lyn L. Antenor presented the purpose of the activity, while Assistant Regional Director Kathrine H. Lotilla offered words of challenge to participants.

The second day focused on developing policy recommendations based on policy analysis. As part of the ways forward, CLMD will continue its monthly Kumustahan sessions to sustain technical assistance and coordination with CID and the Schools Division Offices.

The convergence underscored the importance of collaboration, open communication, and continuous support in ensuring that reforms are understood and effectively carried out in schools across SOCCSKSARGEN.
